reviewMethod: Exact named OpenStreetMap feature, official operator guidance, and a destination-specific licensed campaign photograph.

roger-williams-park-casino.name: Roger Williams Park Casino
roger-williams-park-casino.summary: The Roger Williams Park Casino is the historic 1896 Colonial Revival event building beside the lake and Victorian Rose Garden.
roger-williams-park-casino.cost: Viewing the exterior and surrounding public park is free; indoor access, private events, and rentals follow separate reservations and prices.
roger-williams-park-casino.hours: The surrounding grounds follow the park's 7:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. hours, but the Casino interior is not a general daily walk-in facility and follows booked-event or announced public hours.
roger-williams-park-casino.needToKnow: Casino here means a social gathering house, not gambling. Route to the exact building near the Elmwood Avenue side, and do not rely on it for an open restroom, shelter, or interior visit without a scheduled event.

carousel-village.name: Carousel Village
carousel-village.summary: Carousel Village is the zoo-operated family destination with an indoor carousel and the outdoor fully accessible Hasbro Boundless Playground.
carousel-village.cost: The playground can be used without a park admission charge; carousel rides, food, parties, and special activities have separate prices.
carousel-village.hours: Carousel sessions and indoor services follow the zoo operator's live seasonal schedule. The outdoor playground is described as open year-round, subject to weather, maintenance, and park access.
carousel-village.needToKnow: Check the current carousel schedule before promising children a ride. Public restrooms are available at Carousel Village only during operating hours, and Food Truck Friday is seasonal and weather-dependent.

temple-to-music.name: Temple to Music
temple-to-music.summary: Temple to Music is the monumental open-air performance landmark on Cunliff Lake, used for concerts, gatherings, photographs, and lakefront visits.
temple-to-music.cost: Ordinary outdoor visits are free; formal photography, organized events, and reserved use require approval or permits.
temple-to-music.hours: Outdoor access follows the park's 7:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. hours unless an event, setup, maintenance, or weather condition restricts the lawn or structure.
temple-to-music.needToKnow: Use the exact Temple pin because it is distant from the zoo and Elmwood entrance. A boat ramp is nearby, but lake conditions and boating rules apply; formal photo sessions need a permit.

japanese-garden.name: Japanese Garden
japanese-garden.summary: The Japanese Garden is the 1936 WPA landscape between Carousel Village and the former Seal House, with water, bridges, paths, and a historic stone lantern.
japanese-garden.cost: Casual public garden access is free; formal photo sessions and organized use require a City permit.
japanese-garden.hours: Outdoor access follows Roger Williams Park's 7:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. hours, subject to maintenance, events, ice, high water, and weather.
japanese-garden.needToKnow: The garden is a quiet walking and photography destination, not a playground. Expect bridges, water edges, narrow or uneven paths, and seasonal conditions; use the exact pin rather than the broad park address.

fort-allen-park.name: Fort Allen Park
fort-allen-park.summary: Fort Allen Park is the historic overlook on Eastern Promenade with harbor views, lawns, paths, monuments, and military artifacts.
fort-allen-park.cost: Ordinary public access is free; organized events and reserved or commercial uses can require permits.
fort-allen-park.hours: Outdoor access follows current Portland park hours and posted event, snow, maintenance, and construction restrictions.
fort-allen-park.needToKnow: Fort Allen sits above East End Beach and the lower trail, so use the exact overlook pin. Stairs and slopes connect levels, waterfront wind can be strong, and event or winter conditions may change the easiest accessible route.

eastern-promenade-trail.name: Eastern Promenade Trail
eastern-promenade-trail.boundaryExceptionReason: The official lower waterfront trail is part of the Eastern Promenade visitor corridor but runs below and beyond the mapped upper park-land polygon.
eastern-promenade-trail.summary: Eastern Promenade Trail is the lower waterfront multi-use route connecting the Old Port side, East End Beach, Cutter Street, and the Back Cove direction.
eastern-promenade-trail.cost: Walking and bicycling the public trail are free; nearby parking, boat launch, rail attractions, events, and rentals can cost separately.
eastern-promenade-trail.hours: Use the trail during current Portland park hours and obey temporary event, rail-crossing, storm, snow, ice, construction, and waterfront closure notices.
eastern-promenade-trail.needToKnow: The lower trail and upper Promenade are different elevations. Expect active pedestrian and bicycle traffic, yield at crossings, watch for rail operations near the waterfront, and choose a specific access point instead of the broad park pin.

deering-oaks-pond.name: Deering Oaks Pond
deering-oaks-pond.summary: Deering Oaks Pond and its ornamental fountain form the central water landscape of the historic park.
deering-oaks-pond.cost: Viewing the pond and using ordinary park paths are free; events, field reservations, vendors, and organized activities can charge or require permits.
deering-oaks-pond.hours: Pond access follows current park hours, while fountain operation is seasonal and can stop for weather, maintenance, water-quality work, or winterization.
deering-oaks-pond.needToKnow: The pond and fountain are ornamental, not a splash pad or supervised swimming area. Keep children back from the edge, do not expect the fountain to operate year-round, and use the separate seasonal splash area for water play.

forever-young-treehouse.name: Forever Young Treehouse
forever-young-treehouse.sourceLabel: City of Burlington Parks, Recreation and Waterfront
forever-young-treehouse.summary: Forever Young Treehouse is Oakledge Park's universally accessible elevated play and overlook structure near the picnic shelters.
forever-young-treehouse.cost: Ordinary public use is free, though seasonal park parking charges can apply.
forever-young-treehouse.hours: Use the treehouse during safe public park conditions; it is first-come, first-served and must remain open to the public rather than becoming part of a private reservation.
forever-young-treehouse.needToKnow: The City does not issue exclusive permits for the treehouse. Keep routes and platforms open to other visitors, supervise children, and check for ice, wet decking, maintenance, or event impacts before use.

blanchard-beach.name: Blanchard Beach
blanchard-beach.boundaryExceptionReason: Burlington identifies Blanchard Beach as an Oakledge Park public beach, while its mapped shoreline polygon lies just north of the narrower park-land polygon.
blanchard-beach.sourceLabel: City of Burlington Parks, Recreation and Waterfront
blanchard-beach.summary: Blanchard Beach is Oakledge Park's named Lake Champlain swimming beach on the north side of the park.
blanchard-beach.cost: Beach access itself is public; the City lists Oakledge parking at $3 per hour from May through October 31 for the 2026 season.
blanchard-beach.hours: Use the beach only under current posted park, water-quality, weather, and seasonal facility conditions; beach testing and closure notices can change faster than general park access.
blanchard-beach.needToKnow: Check Burlington's current swim-water status before entering Lake Champlain. Dogs are not allowed on public swimming beaches, and restroom, shelter, rental, and staffed-service availability is seasonal.

oakledge-park-playground.name: Oakledge Park Playground
oakledge-park-playground.sourceLabel: City of Burlington Parks, Recreation and Waterfront
oakledge-park-playground.summary: Oakledge Park Playground is the accessible play area near the park's waterfront paths, shelters, treehouse, courts, and beaches.
oakledge-park-playground.cost: The playground is free to use; seasonal vehicle parking and shelter reservations cost separately.
oakledge-park-playground.hours: Use the outdoor playground during safe public park conditions and obey posted maintenance, ice, severe-weather, and event restrictions.
oakledge-park-playground.needToKnow: Navigate to the playground pin instead of the beach or shelter. The park includes water, bicycle traffic, courts, and multiple activity zones, so supervise children closely and keep accessible routes clear.
